h: Ospreys, Pencils and Stone Circles Nearby
p: The park makes a handy anchor for a day on the quieter, northern side of Keswick. Once you've seen the animals, it's well worth carrying on around Bassenthwaite Lake, which is famous for its ospreys. In season, the viewpoints at Dodd Wood have been a popular spot for watching these huge fish-eating birds, and the Whinlatter Forest visitor centre up the pass has trails, play areas and mountain bike routes through the trees. Animal day, bird day, forest day: you can roll all three into one.

Back in Keswick, there's plenty to keep the family busy on a wet afternoon. The Derwent Pencil Museum tells the story of the graphite mined in Borrowdale and the pencils made from it, and it's quirkier and more fun than it sounds. Keswick Museum covers local history, art and geology, and Theatre by the Lake on the shore of Derwentwater puts on plays through much of the year. Just outside town, Castlerigg Stone Circle stands on a plateau ringed by fells, and it's one of the most atmospheric spots in the whole of the Lakes, especially at sunset.

A few practical tips. Allow a good couple of hours at the wildlife park, more if you catch talks or feeds. Parking in Keswick itself can fill up fast in summer and on bank holidays, so arriving early helps, and having a backup plan for parking saves a lot of circling. And always carry a waterproof. Lakeland weather can be glorious, but it can also turn grey in the blink of an eye.
